input.prompt: A new panel cut from the very same antique hand-painted Srikalahasti kalamkari cotton cloth as the reference image. Copy the reference exactly for: its deep madder red ground, its ecru-and-madder lotus-and-vine scroll border between two thin dotted bands running around all four edges, its fine hand-dotted and cross-hatched fill patterns, its slightly wobbly freehand iron-black kalam lines that vary in thickness, its visible coarse hand-woven cotton weave, slight dye bleed and faint unevenness of dye. Photographed flat and straight-on, the cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge. It must look like a real hand-painted craft textile hanging in a museum, not a digital illustration: no vector look, no comic-book style, no halftone screen dots. Scene inside the border: an afternoon seaside cafe terrace on a green hillside above the sea. Foreground, large and central: a young man and a young woman seated facing each other on either side of a small round table, deep in conversation, each holding one coffee cup, leaning in toward each other. The table is covered by a long tablecloth with a lotus-and-dot kalamkari pattern that falls straight to the floor, and the couple are seen from the waist up above it, so their legs are hidden behind the tablecloth. Both figures drawn strictly like the figures on a Srikalahasti temple cloth: pure side-profile faces, a single large elongated almond eye reaching toward the ear, arched eyebrow, long straight nose, small smiling lips, stylised graceful hands, bodies filled with fine pattern. The young man (left, pure side profile facing right): short black hair, neat short black beard, thin round spectacles seen from the side, a checked shirt in indigo and ecru squares. The young woman (right, pure side profile facing left): long black hair in a single long braid down her back with a small flower, small earring, a simple plain top in myrobalan-turmeric yellow with fine red dots. Each person has exactly two arms and two hands with five fingers. Near the far left and far right edges, much smaller in scale, three friends sit around a low table with small cups, chatting: two on the left, one on the right, also drawn in kalamkari profile style. Behind: a low terrace railing with potted plants, a green dotted hillside with palm trees, then the sea as stylised rolling indigo waves with ecru crests and patterned fish, two small sailboats, and a large round afternoon sun in turmeric yellow ringed by lotus-petal rays against the madder red sky. Palette strictly natural vegetable dyes: deep madder red, brick red, indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green from indigo over yellow, undyed ecru cotton, iron-black. Clothing hems and edges are plain, with no decorative bands or trim. Completely flat, no perspective shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. Exactly five people in total. No text, no letters, no writing, no glyphs, no numbers, no signboard, no menu, no logos, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames.
